name: Rename each command's oclif.ts to a framework-neutral adapter.ts
description:
## Why

Every command directory in `packages/cli/src/commands/` bakes the CLI framework's brand name into a
file name. Each `oclif.ts` is a thin leaf — flag/arg declarations, a real-deps factory, and
delegation to a framework-agnostic `run<Domain>Command` in the sibling `index.ts`, per
[ADR 0054](https://github.com/shoptet/partner-cli/blob/develop/doc/decisions/0054-the-port-to-oclif-keeps-the-wire-and-owns-the-exit-path.md).
The seam is already framework-neutral by design; only the file name isn't. Renaming it to
`adapter.ts` makes the file name describe the _role_ (the framework binding) rather than the
_current_ framework, so a future framework change touches the contents of these files and not their
paths — and, more immediately, not the eight-plus documentation sites that name them by path.

**A correction to the original TODO's premise, measured against the code:** this is not a future
_migration blocker_. `packages/cli/package.json`'s `oclif` block uses
`"commands": { "strategy": "explicit", "target": "./dist/index.js", "identifier": "commands" }` —
oclif imports the hand-built `commands` record from `packages/cli/src/index.ts:205-216` and never
scans the filesystem for command files by path or name. No `tsdown` entry glob, ESLint config, or
`vitest.config.ts` coverage path matches these filenames either (checked; none found). So the code
side is a mechanical, compiler-catchable rename: every reference is a TypeScript module specifier,
and a missed one fails `check:types`. The real cost being paid today is documentation drift across
seven files.

## Scope — the eight files

Confirmed by glob; exactly these, all extending `ShoptetOclifCommand` from
`packages/cli/src/lib/oclif/command.ts`:

File

Exports

`packages/cli/src/commands/build/oclif.ts:69`

`BuildOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/dev/oclif.ts:144`

`DevOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/validate/oclif.ts:88`

`ValidateOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/init/oclif.ts:89`

`InitOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/refresh/oclif.ts:73`

`RefreshOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/update/oclif.ts:78`

`UpdateOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/doctor/oclif.ts:72`

`DoctorOclifCommand`

`packages/cli/src/commands/config/autoupdate/oclif.ts:62,72,82`

`ConfigAutoupdateOn/Off/StatusOclifCommand`

Each `oclif.test.ts` sibling is renamed alongside its subject (`adapter.test.ts`).

## Code references to update

- `packages/cli/src/index.ts:2-8,13` — the registry's eight `./commands/<domain>/oclif.js` imports.
- Eight sibling test imports of `"./oclif.js"`: `init/oclif.test.ts:8`, `validate/oclif.test.ts:7`,
  `update/oclif.test.ts:6`, `config/autoupdate/oclif.test.ts:10`, `refresh/oclif.test.ts:8`,
  `doctor/oclif.test.ts:5`, `dev/oclif.test.ts:5`, `build/oclif.test.ts:6`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/refresh/index.test.ts:21` — imports the autoupdate classes from
  `"../config/autoupdate/oclif.js"`.

## Documentation to update, per CLAUDE.md's same-commit rule

- `doc/contracts.md:250` (prose), `:282` (mermaid node `commands/**/oclif.ts`)
- `doc/overview.md:28` (`commands/dev/oclif.ts`'s `realDevExtraDeps`)
- `doc/cli-reference.md:5` (`packages/cli/src/commands/**/oclif.ts`)
- `doc/decisions/0054-…-port-to-oclif….md` — lines 302, 403, 723, 751, 770, 782, 789, 862, 950, 975
- `doc/decisions/0061-dev-default-port.md` — lines 123, 188, 248, 259
- `.claude/skills/new-command/SKILL.md` — lines 17, 62, 66, 281
- `doc/configuration.md:93` — not in the original TODO list: `commands/update/oclif.ts:64`
  appears in the enumeration of every `process.env` read site.

A historical ADR records a decision as it was made, so where 0054/0061 describe _what was done at
the time_, prefer an added note over rewriting history; where they name a path a reader is expected
to open _today_, update the path.

## Explicitly out of scope

The framework's name also appears in `packages/cli/src/lib/oclif/` (`command.ts`,
`command.test.ts`, `test-support.ts`) and in the `*OclifCommand` class-name suffix itself. This
issue deliberately covers only the eight file names, matching the original request. Widening it to
the directory and the class names is a separate decision — worth raising in review, not assumed
here. Note also that no `adapter.ts` exists anywhere in the repo today: the established vocabulary
is `index.ts` = framework-neutral core, `oclif.ts` = framework binding, so `adapter.ts` is a new
coinage rather than an existing convention being restored.

## Done when

- The eight `oclif.ts` files and their eight `oclif.test.ts` siblings are renamed via `git mv`
  (preserving rename detection), every module specifier updated.
- Every documentation site above is updated in the same commit.
- `pnpm verify` is green, and `--describe` parity still holds for all eight commands.
- No behaviour change: golden envelopes in `packages/test-fixtures/fixtures/envelopes/` are
  byte-identical, and no changeset bump beyond `patch`/empty is owed (internal file layout only, no
  public API change).
